conditional_transfer.common_algebra: Let A be one unital C-star algebra. Let alpha be one target point-norm C0 automorphism group with closed generator delta, and let D be a unital star-subalgebra that is a graph core for delta.
conditional_transfer.thermal_sequences: Let beta_n tend to infinity. For each sign sigma in {+,-}, let alpha_n^sigma be a point-norm C0 group on the same identified algebra A, with generator delta_n^sigma and beta_n-KMS state omega_n^sigma. Require D to lie in every generator domain.
conditional_transfer.generator_and_state_limits: For every A in D, ||delta_n^sigma(A)-delta(A)|| tends to zero, and omega_n^sigma tends weak-star to omega_sigma.
conditional_transfer.differential_kms: With physical time alpha_t=Ad exp(itH/hbar), the strip width is beta_n hbar and Araki's differential KMS inequality is -i beta_n hbar omega_n^sigma(A* delta_n^sigma(A)) >= s(x_n,y_n), where x_n=omega_n^sigma(A*A), y_n=omega_n^sigma(AA*), and s(x,y)=x log(x/y) with the standard extended boundary values.
conditional_transfer.safe_entropy_bound: For x,y>0, log(x/y)>=1-y/x gives s(x,y)>=x-y>=-y. The same lower bound holds at the extended boundary. Hence -i hbar omega_n^sigma(A*delta_n^sigma(A))>=-||A||^2/beta_n.
conditional_transfer.ground_limit: Weak-star state convergence plus norm generator convergence passes the energy form to the limit. The graph-core property extends -i hbar omega_sigma(A*delta(A))>=0 and omega_sigma(delta(A))=0 from D to Dom(delta). Thus both omega_+ and omega_- are algebraic ground states of the same target alpha.
conditional_transfer.parity: Let Theta be an involutive linear star-automorphism with Theta(D)=D. Require omega_n^-=omega_n^+ o Theta and delta_n^- o Theta=Theta o delta_n^+ on D. The limits give omega_-=omega_+ o Theta and delta o Theta=Theta o delta, hence alpha o Theta=Theta o alpha.
conditional_transfer.fixed_separator: Require a fixed selfadjoint Theta-odd B in A with ||B||<=1 and liminf_n omega_n^+(B)>=m_0>0. Then omega_+(B)>=m_0, omega_-(B)<=-m_0, and ||omega_+-omega_-||>=2m_0. The two target ground states are distinct.
conditional_transfer.scope: This is an abstract conditional transfer theorem. It does not construct the common algebra, the finite-temperature identified actions, their generator convergence, or the fixed noncollapsing odd witness for exact Q3.

q3_application_boundary.source_cusp: EXP-000790 supplies a zero-temperature source cusp and parity-related time-zero tangent candidates. Uniform fourth moments can turn the unbounded coordinate order label into a bounded odd truncation, but current authority does not identify those candidates as beta-to-infinity KMS limits on one Hamiltonian-derived common algebra.
q3_application_boundary.thermal_separator: The EXP-000782 finite-beta infrared separator decays to zero along beta-to-infinity and therefore cannot itself serve as the fixed m_0 witness.
q3_application_boundary.missing_inputs: To apply the theorem to exact Q3 one must still prove a noncollapsing common spatial carrier, both phase KMS families on it for beta_n tending to infinity, common-core target-generator convergence, and a fixed bounded odd witness with a uniform sign separation.
q3_application_boundary.gap_boundary: The conclusion is ground-state positivity and distinctness only. A broken-sector GNS gap additionally needs the phasewise Poincare, positive implementation, energy identity, and centered form-core hypotheses isolated by R-167 v3.0.

collapse_negative.algebra: Take A=C([-1,1]), alpha_n^+=alpha_n^-=alpha=id, delta_n^+=delta_n^-=delta=0, D=A, beta_n=n, and Theta(f)(q)=f(-q).
collapse_negative.states: Let omega_n^+=ev_(1/n) and omega_n^-=ev_(-1/n). Every state is beta_n-KMS for the trivial dynamics; these two states are pure, extremal, parity related, and norm-distance two for every n.
collapse_negative.collapse: Both sequences converge weak-star to ev_0. For the fixed odd contraction B(q)=q, omega_n^+(B)=1/n tends to zero, so the uniform separator premise fails exactly.
collapse_negative.consequence: Finite-n distinctness, purity, extremality, parity relation, a common algebra, and even exact common generator equality do not imply distinct beta-to-infinity ground limits without a fixed noncollapsing witness. The fixture does not assume or refute thermodynamic phase separation.
